name: Memphis product
summary: The objects of the Memphis group: bookcases, tables, lamps and ceramics built from bright laminate, terrazzo and coloured glass, in stacked geometric shapes with loud patterns.

philosophy.core_thesis: An object is a toy for the mind: it joins cheap, bright materials with symbols and jokes, and it refuses the rule that good taste is quiet.
design_principles: Build each piece from 3 to 7 simple solids: a cube, a cone, a sphere, a slab and a bar.
Cover a flat plane with plastic laminate in a bold pattern of dots, stripes, squiggles or speckles.
Use 4 or more contrasting colours on one object; set a pastel next to a saturated hue.
Make the form asymmetrical: a bookcase has arms, steps and angled shelves.
Join cheap and rich materials: laminate with terrazzo, or enamel with coloured glass.
Put a visible joint or a colour change on every junction where two solids meet.
Give each object a name and a joke; use it as a sign more than as a tool.
anti_patterns: One neutral colour on the whole object
Natural wood left raw and unpatterned

form.geometry: Stacked cubes, cones, spheres, slabs and bars, joined at angles that break the right angle.
form.silhouette: An asymmetrical totem or a tilted stack with arms, steps and a small top element.
form.edges: Sharp edges on slabs and planes with a radius of 0 to 3 mm; spheres and cones give the only curves.
form.proportion: A bookcase is about 190 cm high and 190 cm wide; a table top is 4 to 6 cm thick on short legs; a lamp has a base of 15 to 25 cm.
form.ornament: All over. The surface is the main part of the design: dots, stripes, squiggles, terrazzo chips and a bold black and white grid.
rules: Each object has 3 to 7 primary solids.
Each large plane carries one pattern.
Each object uses 4 or more colours from 4 different hue groups.
At least 50% of the visible surface carries a printed or pressed pattern.

materials.rule: Laminate and terrazzo make about 60% of the visible surface; glass, ceramic and printed cotton give the rest.

finish.gloss: 30–70 GU on laminate; 80–95 GU on glaze and glass; 5–15 GU on terrazzo
finish.patina: The style wants a new, flat and clean surface; a worn pattern or a chip is a fault.

hardware.section: Rods and legs 12–25 mm; a tube leg or a stem 20–30 mm
hardware.joints: Visible planes joined at angles; a colour change marks each joint.
hardware.handles: A round or a cone knob in a bright colour, or a plain slot cut in the laminate.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A flat square rocker in white or a primary colour; a plain round chrome tap.

palette.strategy: Four or more contrasting colours on each piece: a saturated primary, a candy pastel, black and white, with a terrazzo or squiggle pattern.

manufacture.scale: Small series of a few hundred pieces from Italian workshops, then licensed copies in cheaper laminate.
manufacture.signs: A thin edge band of contrast colour, a printed squiggle on a laminate plane, and a joint where two colours meet.

objects.form: flush rocker on a square plate in bright colour
stacked geometric lamp on a laminate base
armchair with a printed cover on a laminate frame
low table with a terrazzo top on four colour legs
stacking geometric set with banded glaze

emotion.target_response: Surprise and delight: the viewer laughs at a bright, odd object and sees that taste can be a game.

use_cases: product briefs for a Memphis-inspired collection
a prop list for an 1980s set
a pattern study for a laminate range
avoid_when: The room needs calm, quiet or natural objects.
The brief asks for one neutral colour or no pattern.

modifiers.how: Remove the pattern, keep one simple solid in matte white plastic or pale wood.
Fuse the solids into one moulded body with one gloss colour.
Align the solids on a grid, use grey and white, and drop the pattern.

era_blend.note: A reissue keeps the style; a new object keeps the stack of solids and the pattern.
